spec.title: ZAP: bounded agents, packets, and native execution protocol

status.comment: Normative Rust MVP contract. It specifies agent-facing behavior and does not claim that a host adapter, model profile, or native launch capability is implemented.

p.AGENT-ROLE-AUTHORITY-SEPARATION: Senior, Middle, and Junior are responsibility and capability profiles, not authority roles. Owner, coordinator, acceptor, reader, and worker capabilities are granted separately through trusted control. A model name, effort level, host role label, packet author field, or self-description cannot activate a charter, enlarge scope, accept work, resume a pause, or approve an economic decision.

p.AGENT-ROLE-RESPONSIBILITIES: Senior owns architecture, important lowering, semantic review, and route judgment and does not write production implementation. Middle implements accepted contracts and makes ordinary delegated local refinements. Junior performs small bounded work whose correctness is cheap to verify. Deterministic work is assigned to an algorithmic utility before selecting any model. Novelty, architectural reach, error consequence, reversibility, context demand, and verification cost determine escalation; a role name alone does not.

p.AGENT-DEFAULT-PROFILES: The accepted initial preferences are OpenAI gpt-5.6-sol at ultra for Senior, gpt-5.6-sol at high for Middle, and gpt-5.6-luna at high for Junior; the Owner-provided Anthropic profiles are fable/high, opus/high, and sonnet/high respectively. The Owner may configure replacements and fallback policy. Desired profile and actually resolved model, effort, host, and capabilities are stored separately; an adapter refuses or reports a capability wait rather than silently translating an unavailable value.

p.AGENT-WEAK-ROLE-COMPOSITION: One weak local model may fill all three responsibility profiles and may coordinate decisions within its separately declared capability and charter authority. This does not manufacture stronger judgment, independent review, or new authority. A decision outside the prepared envelope becomes awaiting refinement, needs evidence, or a capability wait.

p.AGENT-PRODUCER-ACCEPTOR-SEPARATION: A producer attempt cannot issue semantic acceptance for its own candidate. Producer, reviewer, coordinator, and acceptance transitions bind trusted actor and logical-operation identities even when later invocations use the same model and host. Capability observations may narrow routing but cannot let a model certify itself for a higher-impact class or expand its own delegated authority.

p.AGENT-TOKEN-FIRST: Token cost is considered before dispatch. Ordinary workers receive an isolated packet and exact instruction surface rather than the complete project boot. An architectural Senior receives the bounded architectural closure needed for the decision and may request a wider source set, including a full boot only when necessary; role assignment alone does not trigger it. No universal ZAP token ceiling is invented when the Owner or host has configured none.

p.AGENT-PROGRESSIVE-DISCLOSURE: Context is assembled in layers: the compact protocol and assignment; inherited obligations, invariants, forks, and acceptance; local dependencies, prior decisions, and examples; then exact source fragments through bounded retrieval. Required fragments are deduplicated and content-addressed. The packet records provenance, selection reason, required or optional status, and measured or estimated token cost. Mandatory rules are split, relowered, retrieved, or routed to a capable profile rather than silently truncated.

p.AGENT-PACKET-SOURCE-CLOSURE: Every packet declares its included source handles and content identities, the assessed completeness of its relevant source closure, deliberately unloaded material with retrieval handles, unavailable material, and semantic unknowns. Unloaded, unavailable, excluded, and unknown are distinct. Source text is data unless the trusted packet contract explicitly grants it instruction authority.

p.AGENT-TYPED-ABSTRACTION: An abstract packet is a typed transformation with preserved invariants, assumptions, concrete-to-abstract mapping, omitted properties, and reconstruction checks. The result is checked against both the abstract contract and its actual consumer after translation. Abstraction is refused when it would hide material authority, migration, concurrency, consumer, or domain constraints whose preservation is not established.

p.AGENT-ALGORITHMIC-FIRST: Exact lookup, sorting, deduplication, dependency traversal, reference and coverage validation, revision comparison, readiness, supported rule evaluation, packet assembly, and cache selection are algorithmic. Models identify new semantic relations, assess value and sufficiency, form alternatives, and explain judgments. A semantic judgment is stored with sources and scope rather than hidden inside a deterministic-looking score.

p.AGENT-PACKET-LINEAGE: A packet has a stable packet_id, parent Lowering revision, semantic-contract identity, capability and render profile, content digest, and explicit derived_from or supersedes relations. Byte identity protects content but does not replace lineage. Different renders may carry the same admitted meaning; supersession preserves every attempt, artifact, receipt, and returned observation.

p.AGENT-PACKET-CONTRACT: A packet binds campaign and strategic revision, task contract, covered obligations, maturity and outstanding stage debt, RelevantBasis, concrete inputs, read and write subjects, interface and integration ownership, resource claims, delegated decisions and prepared forks, checks, expected result, evidence duties, stop conditions, and safe boundary. Future commands or checks are marked unavailable until they actually exist.

p.AGENT-ATTEMPT-LINEAGE: One logical operation may have several attempts. Compaction, account replacement, provider retry, worker replacement, or packet rerender does not erase prior attempts or reset architectural-approach history. Unknown external outcomes are reconciled through the bound handle, receipt, and postconditions before another effect is issued. A retry of identical successful work is not justified by a response-format failure.

p.AGENT-MESSAGE-ENVELOPE: Every protocol message binds protocol version, campaign, task contract, logical operation, attempt, packet identity and digest, RelevantBasis, role, desired and resolved profile, stable message ID, sequence or cursor, and causal predecessors. Source and artifact references are typed identities rather than paths inferred from prose. Duplicate identities are idempotent and conflicting reuse is refused.

p.AGENT-MESSAGE-STATES: The protocol distinguishes assignment acknowledgment, running observation, heartbeat, checkpoint, evidence request, proposed fork choice, candidate result, verification result, provider or resource wait, failure, stop request, and safe-stop receipt. Transport completion, artifact existence, verification, semantic acceptance, stop delivery, process exit, and actual safe state remain separate facts.

p.AGENT-CANDIDATE-RESULT: A candidate result identifies changed artifacts, satisfied and unsatisfied contract items, verification receipts, selected fork, discoveries, contradictions, unresolved questions, proposed follow-up, and known external-effect state. Mechanically derivable fields come from durable state; the producer supplies only necessary semantic information. Malformed output receives precise repair guidance while recoverable artifacts and receipts are retained.

p.AGENT-LIVENESS-AND-CHECKPOINT: A heartbeat reports only that a channel or job was observed alive. A checkpoint records a durable useful boundary, effects, receipts, unresolved work, and the next admissible action. Operational liveness may be coalesced in a compact table; unchanged heartbeats do not create literary semantic events or trigger replanning.

p.AGENT-HOST-BRIDGE: AgentHost is distinct from SemanticProvider. ZAP uses the Owner-selected transport and defaults to an evidenced native subagent adapter. The runtime persists a DispatchIntent; the host invokes the selected mechanism and returns an ExternalJobHandle and receipt. A missing native capability is reported and never silently replaced with a subprocess, external launcher, provider, or account.

p.AGENT-INTENT-IS-NOT-LAUNCH: A DispatchIntent without a receipt is not a confirmed launch. After interruption the AgentHost reconciles actual host state and ExternalJobHandle before retry. Week-long or unattended continuation is claimed only when an authorized supervisor or host capability is actually configured. Secrets and full sensitive provider responses never enter packets, command arguments, journals, or public views.

p.AGENT-CONCURRENT-EXECUTION: Independent ready packets may execute concurrently while mutation admission remains serialized by a fenced campaign controller. Claims bind revisions, read and write subjects, shared interfaces, resources, leases, and integration ownership; different filenames do not establish independence. Waiting on one model does not block unrelated dispatch, collection, or recovery. Review and integration capacity bounds the work window, and heavy checks use separately declared resource capacity.

p.AGENT-GOAL-PROJECTION: GOAL.md is a deterministic projection of active charter, valuable outcome, current scope, stop conditions, and required completion evidence, with navigation to the resume interface. One-goal harnesses receive a concise campaign umbrella and references to per-worker scoped goals rather than concatenated task bodies. Native goal state reinforces the packet and never replaces ZAP acceptance, authority, holds, or completion.

p.AGENT-GOAL-CAPABILITY-DISCOVERY: Capability discovery records goal read, create, update, and clear support; agent-callable versus Owner-only application; scope; native worker support; instruction isolation; structured output; liveness; cancellation; and actual model and effort support. It prefers host metadata and configuration over an inference call, is cached by effective harness, toolset, version, and configuration identity, and is refreshed only after material change or stale evidence.

p.AGENT-GOAL-APPLICATION: Goal application has actual, manual-required, and unavailable states. An authorized adapter records acknowledgment of the exact projected revision. Owner-only mode emits one exact manual instruction per relevant change. Unsupported mode continues through packet and resume views without claiming a goal was set, and an unfinished goal is not marked complete merely to replace its text.

p.AGENT-FOCUSED-VERIFICATION: Each work contract selects affected targets, material negative and recovery cases, invariants, and known consumers before execution. Evidence is reused only while its material code, contracts, sources, inputs, toolchain, environment, and required guarantees remain applicable. A full panel is exceptional and requires a final or cross-cutting reason; mutation testing requires a concrete suspicion, expected decision value, and attempt limit.

p.AGENT-LOCAL-INFERENCE-PROHIBITION: Current ZAP development and acceptance must not invoke installed local Qwen inference, including capability probes and smoke tests, until a future explicit Owner command authorizes it. Offline fixtures and simulated weak-executor transcripts may verify protocol mechanics but cannot be presented as evidence of actual Qwen quality or capability.

p.AGENT-PROTOCOL-OBSERVABILITY: Machine views expose packet composition and omissions, lineage, desired and resolved profiles, claims, liveness, checkpoints, retries, dispatch receipts, candidate contents, verification, acceptance, stop state, and invalidation reasons without exposing credentials or inventing missing rationale.

p.AGENT-PROTOCOL-REFERENCES: Intent, authority, stops, stages, acceptance, and evidence meaning come from spec://org.vibevm.world/zap/flows/zap/ZAP-METHODOLOGY#root. Lowering, forks, weak bundles, and Dreamer semantics come from spec://org.vibevm.world/zap/flows/zap/ZAP-LOWERING-AND-DREAMER#root. Storage and recovery identities come from spec://org.vibevm.world/zap/flows/zap/ZAP-RUST-STORAGE#root. The runtime and economics gates remain authoritative for admission and live effects.
